drawings.description: schéma en carré : $V$ descend de $\varphi^*(C)$, et une flèche « $F = 0$ » revient de $\mathbb{D}^*(G)^{(p)}$ vers $\mathbb{D}^*(G)$
drawings.kind: square diagram with V and F = 0
drawings.notes: phi*(omega) -> phi*(omega^p) with phi*(C) written above the arrow, from which a double stroke with a heavy head V comes down; under the two ends "=" signs and D*(G), D*(G)^(p); an arrow F = 0 goes back from D*(G)^(p) to D*(G). The upper right label is placed as the transcription reads it.

drawings.description: page au stylo à bille, occupée pour moitié par des croquis : une région notée $C^1$ contenant des feuilles $\Phi_m$, $\Phi_n$ enroulées, un petit ouvert $U \supset V$ envoyé par $\sigma$ vers $\mathbb{R}^m$ (avec $\mathbb{R}^n$ dessiné dedans) ; ailleurs « $C^0$ », « $\emptyset$ », « $C^{\infty}$ » (surchargé), « $m-n$ », « $n-1$ »
drawings.kind: sheet of sketches: region C^1 with wound leaves, chart sigma to R^m
drawings.notes: Upper half of the sheet (ballpoint and pencil), redrawn on tight crops. Left: the region C^1 (doubled pencil oval) containing the leaf drawn in ink as one curve going back and forth five times (the accordion of a wound leaf), with four faint pencil strokes alongside; Phi_m is written at the top left of the oval, Phi_n inside. The small circle (the open U, which bears no legible letter of its own; a mark inside it may be a U or a second v) with the point and the letter V, and the arrow sigma down to R^m: a pencil cone (apex, one side and three hatchings), R^n the heavy stroke from the apex to the right, with a faint pencil stroke going up from the apex next to the label R^n. Pencil hatchings at the left schematised (one curve, four crossing strokes). Right: C^0 ringed, the empty set, C^infinity overwritten (label only), the doubled lens crossed by two heavy strokes, the ink arc at the right edge and n-1 beside it, and the faint pencil links (C^1 to the lens, C^1 to a small loop, the lens down to the big oval). The ink oval round the formulas sigma(V) = sigma(U) cap R^n and A_0 = {...} and the two pencil ovals inside it are drawn; the formulas, V_i subset U_i and the line "1) Familles canoniques C^r" (whose ink frame is drawn, cut by the crop) are text of the transcription. Still differs: the pencil doublings of every oval are drawn once, the pencil leaves and hatchings are schematic. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: à droite, un croquis : deux ouverts $U_1$, $U_2$ traversés par une sous-variété (trait épais) le long de laquelle sont $V_1$, $V_2$ ; $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$ les envoient dans $\mathbb{R}^m$, où $\sigma_1(V_1)$ et $\sigma_2(V_2)$ sont posés sur $\mathbb{R}^n$
drawings.kind: two charts U1, U2 along a submanifold, sent by sigma1, sigma2 to R^m
drawings.notes: Two open sets U_1 and U_2 (circles) crossed by a submanifold (thick curve) along which lie V_1 and V_2 (smaller circles); sigma_1 and sigma_2 send them down into R^m, drawn twice: on the left an axis with sigma_1(V_1) set on R^n, on the right sigma_2(V_2) on R^n. The small labels inside the lower ovals are left out.

drawings.description: feuillet quadrillé tenu en largeur, au crayon. En haut à gauche, sous « $n/17$ », sept petites lignes brisées, une par ligne (« $n = 1, 2, 3$ », « $n = 4$ », « $n = 5$ », « $n = 6$ », « $n = 7, \dots, 13$ », « $n = 14$ », « $n = 15, 16$ »), et la colonne « $\nu$ » : $1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 2$. Au centre, un axe horizontal gradué de 1 à 18 et, à son extrémité droite, un axe vertical gradué de 1 à 16 ; deux longues droites presque parallèles montent de la gauche de l'axe jusqu'au coin supérieur droit, des points marqués le long ; à droite, un faisceau de seize segments de pentes décroissantes aboutit aux seize graduations de l'axe vertical.
drawings.kind: whole-page pencil graph on squared paper (lines of slope n/17, small broken lines)
drawings.notes: Whole page, faint pencil on squared paper held lengthwise. Drawn: the horizontal axis with its graduations 1 to 18; the vertical axis at abscissa 18 with its graduations 1 to 16 and a dot at each level 2 to 16 (levels measured on the page: one square = 3.59 units vertically, level n at y = -61.4 + 3.59 n; the axis itself runs 0.8 unit below level 0); the horizontal line of level 1 from the origin to the vertical axis; the two long lines from the origin and from the next lattice point to the upper right corner, where they meet; eight marked points along the second; the fan at the right: one segment to each level 3 to 16 (none to level 2), each from the point where it starts on the page (short heavy strokes to 16, 15, 12, 9, 8, 7, 5; longer, fainter ones to 14, 13, 11, 10, 6, 4, 3); at the top left the seven small broken lines with their labels n = ..., the heading n/17 and the column headed nu (1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 2). Left out: the inequalities between fractions written all round the graph (they are in the transcription), « 2533 > 285 », the scribble at the top right, the ruling of the paper, further faint lattice dots in the middle of the sheet and the faint doublings of several segments of the fan. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 300 dpi colour render: the graduations, dots and fan ends of the vertical axis were 0.7 to 1 unit low and the fan had been drawn as uniform pieces of the lines from the origin to (18, n), which the page does not show (the segments have different lengths and slopes); corrected from the page. Still differs: the small broken lines at the top left and the starting points of the faint fan segments are read to about 1 unit; where two faint strokes run to one level only one is drawn. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: même papier, au crayon : un axe vertical et un axe horizontal tracé jusqu'à l'abscisse 16 (petite croix) ; une droite de l'origine au point $(16, 14)$ et une droite du point $(1, 0)$ au point $(16, 13)$ ; un court segment de l'origine au point $(2, 1)$ ; des points marqués aux nœuds du quadrillage entre les deux droites.
drawings.kind: pencil graph on squared paper (two lines of slopes 14/16 and 13/15)
drawings.notes: Faint pencil on the same squared paper. Drawn on the lattice measured on the page (one square = 3.55 units across, 3.6 up; origin at (17.7, -58.4)): the vertical axis; the horizontal axis as far as abscissa 16, with the small cross at its end; the line from the origin to (16, 14) (slope 7/8, cf. « 14/16 = 7/8 » on the page) and the heavy line from (1, 0) to the same point (16, 14); the short segment from the origin to (2, 1); a shorter heavy line ending at (16, 13), which starts about (12, 10) and is not continued below; the marked points (2,1), (3,2), (4,3), (5,4), (6,5), (7,6), (8,7), (10,8). Left out: the three inequalities at the right (text), a faint smudge at the upper left, the ruling, faint doublings of the two long lines. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 300 dpi colour render: the second long line had been drawn from (1, 0) to (16, 13) with slope 13/15, where the page has it end at (16, 14) beside the first one; the stroke ending at (16, 13) is a separate short line; corrected. Still differs: the dot at (10, 8) is faint and its place doubtful; faint doublings near the origin not drawn. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: même papier, tenu en hauteur, au crayon. En haut : un axe horizontal de seize carreaux, deux droites issues de l'origine et du point $(1, 0)$ qui se rejoignent à l'abscisse 16, des points marqués le long. En bas : d'une seconde origine et du point voisin partent cinq droites de pentes décroissantes, la plus haute épaisse et brisée au départ, aboutissant à une verticale d'abscisse 16 marquée de points.
drawings.kind: two pencil graphs on squared paper (pencils of lines of rational slopes)
drawings.notes: Pencil on the same paper held upright. Upper graph, on a computed lattice (one square = 4.6 units): the horizontal axis of 16 squares, a short vertical tick at the origin, a thin line from the origin and a heavy line from (1, 0) meeting at abscissa 16 (height about 13), the short segment from the origin to (2, 1), seven marked points. Lower graph: the vertical at abscissa 16 with its dots; from the origin a heavy line, broken at its start, to height about 11, and four more lines to heights about 8, 7, 4 and 2; each is doubled by a faint line from the neighbouring point (1, 0); one faint line overshoots the vertical. Left out: the fractions written on the page (text), the ruling, several further faint lines of the lower pencil between the first and the third line, and faint lattice dots. Still differs: the note of the transcription counts six lines in the lower pencil, five directions are drawn here (the faint ones between are not separated on a 200 dpi render); the end heights are approximate. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 300 dpi colour render: the upper graph, the end heights of the lower pencil and the dots of the vertical match the page within about half a unit; in the lower pencil the heavy line from the origin is straighter on the page than drawn (the broken course via the third square is a fainter stroke) and the line from (1, 0) to the heavy end runs about 1 unit low near its start. Not corrected further. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
